newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish PM gets heart treatment in Danish hospital.
newsitem.headline: Finnish PM gets heart treatment in Danish hospital.

text.p: Finnish Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen had hospital treatment in Copenhagen on Tuesday for a heart rhythm problem, Finland's government said.
An official statement said he was later released by doctors in the Danish capital and would return to Helsinki.
A former swimmer and waterpolo player, Lipponen, 55, has generally been in good health since becoming prime minister in April 1995.
In June this year, he missed a European Union summit due to a stone in the urinary tract, a painful but not dangerous condition.

"Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen was being treated today at the Copenhagen central hospital due to a heart rhythm disturbance. (He) was released from hospital in the afternoon to return home and he will be back at work on Wednesday," the government said.
Lipponen was in Denmark to attend a meeting of the Nordic Council in Copenhagen.
An official at the prime minister's office said Lipponen was scheduled to return to Helsinki on a flight due at 1835 local time (1635 GMT).
Lipponen was already due to return on that flight, the official said.
He said he did not know whether an ambulance would be on standby at the airport, or whether other special arrangements would be made.
